w-nino-franco-rustico.pitch: It's a crisp, dry Prosecco from the steep hills of Valdobbiadene, the best part of the region. Light, fresh and full of green apple and pear, it's the perfect way to start.
w-nino-franco-rustico.taste: Green apple, pear and white flowers, with fine bubbles and a clean, dry finish.
w-nino-franco-rustico.grape: Glera is Prosecco's grape: light, fruity and floral rather than toasty.
w-nino-franco-rustico.place: Valdobbiadene is in the hills of the Veneto in north-east Italy; Superiore DOCG is the higher tier of Prosecco, from these hillsides.

dishes.why: Its bubbles and freshness lift the creamy burrata without weighing it down.

alts.when: a still white with the same freshness
something pink and dry by the glass

qs.q: What grape is the Nino Franco Rustico Prosecco made from?
qs.why: Glera is the grape of Prosecco.

qs.q: How does the Nino Franco Rustico taste?
opts: Dry, with green apple and pear
qs.why: Rustico is a dry, fresh Prosecco: fruit and flowers rather than toast.

qs.q: Which Italian region is the Nino Franco Rustico from?
qs.why: Valdobbiadene sits in the hills of the Veneto, north of Venice.

qs.q: At what temperature do we serve the Nino Franco Rustico?
qs.why: Sparkling wine is served well chilled, about 6-8°C, to keep the bubbles lively.

qs.q: A guest wants a glass of something sparkling while they look at the menu, and says they don't like sweet wine. What do you suggest and how do you describe it?
key: the Nino Franco Rustico Prosecco by the glass
it is dry
fresh green apple and pear
qs.why: Rustico is dry and fresh, the ideal aperitif for someone avoiding sweetness.

qs.q: What grape is the Nino Franco Rustico made from, and what grape is the Domaine Laroche Chablis made from?
acc: prosecco is glera, chablis is chardonnay
qs.why: Prosecco is Glera; Chablis is always Chardonnay.

w-laroche-chablis.pitch: It's a classic Chablis: pure Chardonnay from the cool north of Burgundy, crisp and mineral with lemon and green apple. If you like fresh whites without oak, this is the one.
w-laroche-chablis.taste: Lemon, green apple and a stony, mineral freshness, with no oaky vanilla.
w-laroche-chablis.grape: Chardonnay here is grown in a cool climate, so it stays lean and citrusy rather than rich and buttery.
w-laroche-chablis.place: Chablis is the northernmost part of Burgundy, cool enough that its wines are known for crisp acidity and minerality.

dishes.why: Its crisp acidity cuts the brown butter while staying gentle enough for sweet scallops.
Fresh enough to cut the cream, and Chardonnay loves chicken.

alts.when: more zesty and aromatic, by the bottle
a little cheaper by the glass, with a peppery twist

qs.q: What grape is the Domaine Laroche Chablis made from?
qs.why: All white Chablis is Chardonnay.

qs.q: Which part of France is the Domaine Laroche Chablis from?
qs.why: Chablis is Burgundy's northernmost district.

qs.q: How would you describe the style of the Domaine Laroche Chablis in a few words?
qs.why: Cool-climate Chardonnay: crisp, citrusy and mineral, without oak's vanilla.

qs.q: What do we pour the Domaine Laroche Chablis by the glass for?
qs.why: It's £13 a glass and £58 a bottle.

qs.q: A guest ordering the scallops asks for a white that won't overpower them. What do you recommend and why?
key: the Domaine Laroche Chablis
crisp acidity cuts the brown butter
light enough not to overpower the scallops
qs.why: Chablis's freshness meets the brown butter without masking delicate scallops.

qs.q: A guest likes Chardonnay but wants something more aromatic. Which white on our list do you move them to from the Chablis?
qs.why: Sancerre's Sauvignon Blanc is more aromatic and zesty than Chablis's Chardonnay.

w-jolivet-sancerre.pitch: This is Sancerre, Sauvignon Blanc at its most elegant: zesty citrus, gooseberry and a flinty edge. It's bright and refreshing, and it's brilliant with goat's cheese.
w-jolivet-sancerre.taste: Grapefruit, lime and gooseberry, with a flinty, mineral finish.
w-jolivet-sancerre.grape: Sauvignon Blanc gives zesty citrus and green, grassy notes.
w-jolivet-sancerre.place: Sancerre is in the eastern Loire Valley, where chalky and flinty soils give the wine its mineral edge.

dishes.dish: Goat's cheese tart, red onion marmalade
dishes.why: Goat's cheese and Sancerre are a famous match from the same part of France: the acidity meets the cheese's tang.

alts.when: rounder and less aromatic, also by the glass
by the glass, with a peppery note

qs.q: What grape is the Pascal Jolivet Sancerre made from?
qs.why: White Sancerre is always Sauvignon Blanc.

qs.q: Which dish on our menu is the classic match for the Pascal Jolivet Sancerre?
opts: Goat's cheese tart, red onion marmalade
Braised lamb shoulder, white beans, rosemary
qs.why: Goat's cheese and Sancerre is a classic Loire pairing.

qs.q: Which French wine region is the Pascal Jolivet Sancerre from?
qs.why: Sancerre is in the eastern Loire Valley.

qs.q: Name two flavours you can promise a guest in the Pascal Jolivet Sancerre.
qs.why: Expect grapefruit, lime and gooseberry with a flinty finish.

qs.q: A guest ordering the goat's cheese tart wants a bottle of white. What do you suggest and what do you say about it?
key: the Pascal Jolivet Sancerre
its acidity meets the tang of the goat's cheese
zesty citrus and gooseberry
qs.why: Sancerre's acidity and the cheese's tang are made for each other.

qs.q: Both the Sancerre and the Chablis are crisp French whites. Which is more aromatic, with gooseberry and grapefruit?
qs.why: Sauvignon Blanc is the aromatic one; Chablis's Chardonnay is quieter and more mineral.

w-brundlmayer-gruner.pitch: It's Austria's signature white: fresh and crisp with green apple, citrus and a little twist of white pepper. A lovely, food-friendly glass if you fancy something different.
w-brundlmayer-gruner.taste: Green apple and lemon with a hint of white pepper, fresh and dry.
w-brundlmayer-gruner.grape: Grüner Veltliner is Austria's most planted grape, known for its peppery spice and freshness.
w-brundlmayer-gruner.place: Kamptal is one of Austria's best regions for Grüner Veltliner, along the Danube west of Vienna.

dishes.why: Its freshness and peppery note pick up the basil and tomatoes.

dishes.dish: Goat's cheese tart, red onion marmalade
dishes.why: Crisp enough for the cheese, by the glass.

alts.when: a classic French alternative by the glass

qs.q: Which country is the Bründlmayer Grüner Veltliner from?
qs.why: Grüner Veltliner is Austria's signature grape; Kamptal is in Austria.

qs.q: What spicy note is Grüner Veltliner known for?
qs.why: Grüner Veltliner is famous for a twist of white pepper.

qs.q: What grape is the Bründlmayer Kamptal Terrassen made from?
qs.why: It's 100% Grüner Veltliner.

qs.q: What's the glass price of the Bründlmayer Grüner Veltliner?
qs.why: £11 a glass, £49 a bottle.

qs.q: A guest who usually drinks Pinot Grigio wants to try something new by the glass with the burrata. What do you suggest and how do you sell it?
key: the Bründlmayer Grüner Veltliner
fresh and crisp like Pinot Grigio but with more character
green apple and a twist of white pepper
qs.why: Grüner is the easy step up from Pinot Grigio: just as fresh, with more flavour.

qs.q: Which by-the-glass white has a peppery note: the Bründlmayer or the Laroche Chablis?
qs.why: White pepper is Grüner Veltliner's signature; Chablis is mineral and citrusy.

w-minuty-m.pitch: This is a classic pale Provence rosé: dry, delicate and refreshing with strawberry and citrus. Summer in a glass, and lovely with lighter starters.
w-minuty-m.taste: Strawberry, peach and citrus, light and dry.
w-minuty-m.grape: Provence rosé is usually a blend led by Grenache with Cinsault, giving red-berry fruit and a pale colour.
w-minuty-m.place: Côtes de Provence is in the south of France, the home of pale, dry rosé.

dishes.why: Dry rosé and tomatoes are a natural match, fresh enough for the creamy burrata.

qs.q: How would you describe the M de Minuty rosé to a guest?
qs.why: Provence rosé is famously pale and dry.

qs.q: Which grape usually leads a Côtes de Provence rosé like the M de Minuty?
qs.why: Provence rosé is usually Grenache-led with Cinsault.

qs.q: Which region of France is the M de Minuty rosé from?
qs.why: It's a Côtes de Provence rosé.

qs.q: Is the M de Minuty rosé sweet or dry?
qs.why: Provence rosé is dry, whatever its pale pink colour suggests.

qs.q: A guest worries rosé will be sweet but wants a pink wine with the burrata. What do you say?
key: the M de Minuty Côtes de Provence
it is dry
fresh strawberry and citrus that suits tomatoes and burrata
qs.why: Reassure them: Provence rosé is dry, and its freshness suits the starter.

qs.q: A guest with the burrata wants a glass. Which suits it: the M de Minuty rosé or the Catena Malbec?
qs.why: A dry rosé suits tomatoes and burrata; the Malbec's tannin would trample them.

w-jadot-bourgogne.pitch: This is red Burgundy, Pinot Noir: light, silky and full of red cherry and raspberry. It's the red to choose when you want something elegant rather than heavy.
w-jadot-bourgogne.taste: Red cherry and raspberry, silky and light, with gentle tannin.
w-jadot-bourgogne.grape: Pinot Noir is a thin-skinned grape that makes light, fragrant reds with soft tannin.
w-jadot-bourgogne.place: Burgundy is Pinot Noir's home in eastern France; Bourgogne is its regional level.

dishes.why: Light enough for chicken, and Pinot Noir's earthiness loves the morels.

qs.q: What grape is the Louis Jadot Bourgogne made from?
qs.why: Red Bourgogne is Pinot Noir.

qs.q: Which dish on our menu suits the Louis Jadot Pinot Noir best?
opts: Goat's cheese tart, red onion marmalade
qs.why: Pinot Noir's lightness and earthiness suit chicken and mushrooms.

qs.q: How would you describe the body of the Louis Jadot Bourgogne Pinot Noir?
qs.why: Pinot Noir is one of the lightest reds.

qs.q: At what temperature do we serve the Louis Jadot Bourgogne?
qs.why: Light reds taste best slightly cool, around 14-16°C.

qs.q: A guest having the roast chicken wants a red but says big reds are too heavy for them. What do you suggest and why?
key: the Louis Jadot Bourgogne Pinot Noir
light with soft tannin
its earthy notes suit the morels
qs.why: Pinot Noir is light and silky, and its earthiness meets the morels.

qs.q: Which of our reds is lighter: the Louis Jadot Bourgogne or the Catena Malbec?
qs.why: Pinot Noir is light and silky; Malbec is fuller and plummier.

w-catena-malbec.pitch: A rich, smooth Malbec from high in the Andes: plum, blackberry and a hint of violet with soft tannins. It's the one for steak.
w-catena-malbec.taste: Plum, blackberry and violet, smooth and full.
w-catena-malbec.grape: Malbec gives dark plum fruit, deep colour and soft, rounded tannins.
w-catena-malbec.place: Mendoza in Argentina grows Malbec at high altitude, where sunny days and cool nights keep the fruit ripe and fresh.

dishes.why: Its dark fruit and tannin stand up to the steak's char and richness.

alts.when: more savoury and aged, by the bottle

qs.q: Which country is the Catena Malbec from?
qs.why: Catena is in Mendoza, Argentina.

qs.q: Which dish on our menu is the classic match for the Catena Malbec?
qs.why: Malbec with steak is a classic.

qs.q: Name the Argentine region the Catena Malbec comes from.
qs.why: Mendoza is Argentina's main wine region, high in the Andes foothills.

qs.q: Name two flavours you can promise a guest in the Catena Malbec.
qs.why: Plum, blackberry and a floral hint of violet.

qs.q: A guest ordering the sirloin asks for a red by the glass. What do you suggest and how do you describe it?
key: the Catena Malbec by the glass
rich and smooth with plum and blackberry
stands up to the steak
qs.why: Malbec's dark fruit and tannin match the steak, and it's by the glass.

qs.q: Both suit the sirloin. Which is more savoury and aged: the Catena Malbec or the Viña Ardanza Reserva?
qs.why: Ardanza is an aged Rioja Reserva, savoury and mellow; Malbec is fruitier and younger.

w-guigal-cdr.pitch: A warm, spicy red from the southern Rhône: raspberry, blackberry and a touch of pepper and herbs. Easy to love and great value.
w-guigal-cdr.taste: Red and black berries, black pepper and dried herbs, medium-bodied.
w-guigal-cdr.grape: This house's blend is documented: Grenache for juicy fruit, Syrah for pepper and colour, Mourvèdre for depth.
w-guigal-cdr.place: Côtes du Rhône is the wide southern Rhône Valley, warm and sunny, known for Grenache-led blends.

dishes.dish: Braised lamb shoulder, white beans, rosemary
dishes.why: Its pepper and herbs echo the rosemary, and it's soft enough for slow-cooked lamb.

alts.when: a step up, aged and savoury

qs.q: Which grape leads the Guigal Côtes du Rhône blend?
qs.why: Southern Rhône reds are Grenache-led, with Syrah and Mourvèdre.

qs.q: What does the Guigal Côtes du Rhône taste of, beyond fruit?
qs.why: Syrah and the warm south give pepper and herby notes.

qs.q: Name the three grapes in the Guigal Côtes du Rhône.
qs.why: Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre: the southern Rhône trio.

qs.q: Which French river valley is the Guigal Côtes du Rhône from?
qs.why: It's from the southern Rhône Valley.

qs.q: A table having the lamb shoulder wants a red bottle under £50. What do you suggest and why?
key: the Guigal Côtes du Rhône at £46
pepper and herbs echo the rosemary
soft enough for slow-cooked lamb
qs.why: It's under £50 and its herbs and spice suit the lamb.

qs.q: Which red is spicier with black pepper: the Guigal Côtes du Rhône or the Louis Jadot Bourgogne?
qs.why: Syrah in the blend brings pepper; Pinot Noir is about red fruit.

w-ardanza-reserva.pitch: One of Rioja's classics, aged for years before release: mellow red fruit, vanilla and spice from American oak, smooth and savoury. A special bottle for the lamb or the steak.
w-ardanza-reserva.taste: Dried red cherry, vanilla, sweet spice and leather, smooth and mellow.
w-ardanza-reserva.grape: Not printed on the label, but this house's blend is known: Tempranillo for structure and red fruit, with Garnacha for warmth.
w-ardanza-reserva.place: Rioja in northern Spain; a Reserva has to age for years, part of it in oak, before it's sold.

dishes.dish: Braised lamb shoulder, white beans, rosemary
dishes.why: Rioja and lamb are a Spanish classic: the wine's mellow fruit and spice suit the slow-cooked meat.
Smooth tannin and savoury depth for the aged beef.

qs.q: What grape leads the Viña Ardanza Reserva?
qs.why: Tempranillo leads, with Garnacha.

qs.q: Where does the vanilla and spice in the Viña Ardanza Reserva come from?
qs.why: American oak gives Rioja its vanilla and sweet spice.

qs.q: Which country is the Viña Ardanza Reserva from?
qs.why: It's a Rioja, from northern Spain.

qs.q: How long do we decant the Viña Ardanza Reserva for?
qs.why: Half an hour lets an aged Reserva open up.

qs.q: A table celebrating with the lamb shoulder want a special red bottle. What do you suggest and how do you describe it?
key: the Viña Ardanza Reserva
an aged Rioja: mellow, smooth, vanilla and spice
a classic match for lamb
qs.why: Rioja Reserva and lamb is a classic, and Ardanza is the list's special red.

qs.q: Which of our reds has been aged longer before release: the Viña Ardanza Reserva or the Catena Malbec?
qs.why: A Rioja Reserva must age for years before release; the Malbec is a young, fruity wine.

w-lions-suduiraut.pitch: It's Sauternes, the famous sweet wine of Bordeaux: honey, apricot and orange peel, rich but with fresh acidity so it never cloys. Wonderful with the lemon tart.
w-lions-suduiraut.taste: Honey, apricot and candied orange, sweet and rich with fresh acidity.
w-lions-suduiraut.grape: Sémillon gives the richness and Sauvignon Blanc the freshness.
w-lions-suduiraut.place: Sauternes, in Bordeaux, makes sweet wine from grapes shrivelled by noble rot (botrytis), which concentrates their sugar.

dishes.why: The wine must be at least as sweet as the dessert; its acidity matches the lemon.

qs.q: What makes Sauternes like the Lions de Suduiraut so sweet?
opts: Noble rot shrivels the grapes and concentrates the sugar
The grapes are frozen on the vine
It is blended with grape juice
qs.why: Botrytis, or noble rot, concentrates the grapes' sugar.

qs.q: Which region is the Lions de Suduiraut from?
qs.why: Sauternes is in Bordeaux.

qs.q: What's the main grape in Sauternes like the Lions de Suduiraut?
qs.why: Sémillon leads, with Sauvignon Blanc.

qs.q: How do we sell the Lions de Suduiraut by the glass?
qs.why: A 75ml glass at £9, or a half bottle at £55.

qs.q: A guest ordering the lemon tart asks if there's a wine to go with it. What do you suggest and why?
key: the Lions de Suduiraut Sauternes by the glass
it must be as sweet as the dessert
its acidity matches the lemon
qs.why: A dessert wine should be at least as sweet as the dessert; Sauternes's acidity meets the lemon.

qs.q: Which of our wines is sweet: the Lions de Suduiraut or the Nino Franco Rustico?
qs.why: Sauternes is sweet; the Rustico Prosecco is dry.
